beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:hushed, tender]About five thousand three hundred years ago, in what is now the Sahara ^desert@noun, a woman and two children were buried together, in an ^embrace.

[d:calm][act:plain, orienting]The place is ^Gobero, in ^Niger, today a sea of sand on the southern edge of the ^Sahara. [act:storytelling]In {2000|two thousand}, a team led by Paul ^Sereno found a cemetery there, beside a lake that has since ^vanished.

[d:build][go:2|0][act:impressed]About two hundred ^burials. [p:0.93][act:vivid]And around them, the bones of fish, ^hippos and ^crocodiles. [act:explaining, clear]Hippos and crocodiles need deep water all year ^round. [act:explaining, plain][tune:fall]So this was a real ^lake, up to about three kilometres ^wide.

[d:build][act:building, precise]The first people buried here are called the ^Kiffian. [act:vivid]From about {7700|seventy-seven hundred} BCE, they fished the lake with ^harpoons. [act:grave]Then came a long dry spell, and the lake ^emptied. [p:0.93][act:grave, quiet][tune:fall]For about a thousand years, no one was buried ^here.
[d:build][act:the change]When the water came back, so did the ^burials. [act:the change, precise]But they looked ^different. [act:steady]These people are called the ^Tenerians, and they kept ^cattle.

[d:build][act:tender, careful]The embrace belongs to this second, Tenerian ^phase. [p:0.93][act:gentle, explaining]Pollen grains are tiny and tough, and each kind of plant has its own ^shape, like a ^signature. [act:gentle][tune:fall]Here, pollen suggests that flowers were laid in the ^grave.

[d:reveal][act:fair, even]In {2008|two thousand eight}, the team saw two different ^peoples, a thousand years ^apart. [p:0.93][act:curious, the method]But how can you tell who is ^related? [act:explaining, a simple picture]One clue is ^teeth: their little bumps and grooves run in families, a bit like the shape of a ^nose. [act:the twist, precise]In {2026|twenty twenty-six}, a study of their teeth, with Sereno as a co-author, found the two groups hard to tell ^apart.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, even][tune:rise]One people, or ^two? [act:the verdict, measured][tune:fall]*Open ^question*. [act:fair]Ancient DNA could ^settle it, if any survives the desert@noun ^heat.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:the last word, warm, gentle][tune:fall]Either way, someone loved ^them.
